correctness.rationale: An exactly conserved affine offset reduces the two-dimensional map to u_{j+1}=u_j[1-q(u_j+d)]. For bounded t=qn d, the reciprocal variable h_j=1/(n u_j) obeys an exact Euler-type recurrence with denominator bounded below by 1-a. Discrete Gronwall bounds h_j and a reciprocal inequality gives sum_{j<n}u_j=O(log n), making the cumulative Euler error O(log n/n). The limiting ODE has a strictly positive solution, yielding both rescaled coordinates uniformly on compact initial slices. The initial-square affine Jacobian q/a and t=qn d give an exact 1/a coarea factor. Compact support restricts t, allowing the endpoint slices to be discarded by area. These steps prove the infinite-limit statement; finite-generation checker runs corroborate rather than certify it.

value.rationale: The initial-square rare-event intensity is a natural finite-generation statistic for a two-sex population model at the intersection of two fixed-point branches. It resolves how a small but nonvanishing fraction O(1/n) of starting compositions has both minority populations visible on the scale 1/n, including the universal nonlinear joint dependence and exact coefficient U/a. The full distribution is not supplied by qualitative convergence or a generic scalar 1/n exponent, and supports finite-generation near-critical population inference.
